articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Bellwood
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Bellwood Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for basketball court along Sawmill Avenue, with work expected to start in September.

Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. Kiera Schaefer, who has lived in Bellwood for 30 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Arthur Kaczmarek, 78, Neighborhood Baker
articles.deck: Friends remember Arthur Kaczmarek for the many years of service to Lower Millrace.
body: Arthur Kaczmarek died in June at home on Mill Road, at the age of 78. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Lower Millrace. Born in Lower Millrace in the years after the war, Arthur Kaczmarek spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Arthur Kaczmarek died in June at home on Mill Road, at the age of 78. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Footpath Repair Near Cedar Hollow
articles.deck: The vote came after 9 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: Councilmember Eleanor Moffat asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000.
The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 9 weeks once it starts in June.

Residents of Cedar Hollow said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Library Adds Seasonal Farmers Market This Spring
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
The event will be held at the Cedar Hollow Pavilion, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Tuesday.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Adds Playground Upgrade to Spring Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in December and is open to all students in grade 4 and up.
body: Students will meet on Sunday afternoons in the Eastgate community hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
The board will review the results at the end of the spring term.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for December.
